summary: DONE is correct. The multi-second stall on the whole server is gone. Statistics rows are read in one WAL read transaction on a read-only worker_thread connection, which has its own semaphore. Only threads with new events or changed meta are re-read, using json_each scopes. Per-thread partials are persisted, so the first open after a restart is incremental too. The RPC serves the previous snapshot after 250 ms and lets the refresh finish. The web hook keeps a module-level snapshot. Aggregation chunks yield through setImmediate (Effect 4.0.2 MixedScheduler), so I/O runs between chunks. Production servers run on Node (CLI and Electron-as-node), so the worker is actually used; the main-connection fallback is only for Bun, :memory: or a crashed worker. I checked the invariant behind incremental refresh: thread-scoped rows are written only by the projection pipeline, ThreadFork and ProviderRuntimeIngestion only read them, and every event advances every projector cursor. It holds. The auditor missed one real defect in the client cache (proposal 4) and some smaller server edge cases; they are listed in fixDefects.

evidence.note: reader = SqliteReadClient or the main client. readRows runs inside reader.withTransaction (603-605), so the writer semaphore is not held.
The worker transactionAcquirer uses its own Semaphore(1). Its only users are StatisticsQuery and DailyRecapQuery, so a full statistics read cannot hold up hot paths.
SqliteReadClientLayer.layer(dbPath) is in the runtime layer. apps/server/package.json runs the server with node; the desktop uses ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:111).
Dirty set = threads with events after coveredSequence, plus threads whose metaKey changed. Rebuilds fully on an external commit, a sequence regression, or more than max(256, threads/4) dirty threads.
Every projector cursor is advanced on every event, so projectedSequence (MIN over thread-scoped projectors) cannot get stuck and force rebuilds.
Effect.yieldNow every 256 threads. MixedScheduler uses setImmediate (effect 4.0.2 dist/Scheduler.js:112), so the event loop gets control back.
DEFECT: lastSnapshot is one module-level value, not keyed by environment. The SharedRequests key is the constant "statistics".
The error panel shows only when snapshot is null. The data is labelled with getPrimaryKnownEnvironment()?.label, so a carried-over snapshot appears under the current node's name.

clearWebHostedNodeScopedState and clearWebHostedAccountScopedState do not clear the statistics snapshot. usageSummaryCache, by contrast, is keyed per environment (packages/client-runtime/src/usage/summaryCache.ts:68-92).

restored=true is set before the first refresh succeeds. With no stale snapshot, the first refresh runs in the RPC fiber, so a WS disconnect throws away the restored partials and the next open does a full rebuild.
If the joined background refresh fails inside the wait window, the error is returned (orDie in statisticsRpc.ts:24) even though a stale snapshot exists.

Persisted partials are keyed on MAX(migration_id). Migrations 087-090 landed on 2026-10-12..14, so the first open after most upgrades does a full rebuild: reads off-thread, but structured-clone and Schema decode of all rows (409-415) happen in one main-thread step.

fixDefects: 1) Client cache is not scoped to an environment (introduced in 60633eff3). useStatistics.ts:21 keeps one module-level lastSnapshot and uses the constant SharedRequests key "statistics". The hosted node-switch and account teardown catalogs (hostedHub/environment.ts:29,58) never clear it. A hosted user who opens Activity on node A, switches to node B in the Hub directory and reopens Activity sees A's projects, token usage and PR titles under B's label (ActivityView.tsx:87,114) until B answers. If B's request fails, A's data stays on screen with no error, because the error panel only renders when snapshot is null (ActivityView.tsx:70, StatisticsPanel.tsx:91). After an in-page account switch (passkey sign-in, handled at hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:737-750 without a reload), the previous account's owner-only statistics are painted the same way. 2) StatisticsQuery.ts:599-602 sets restored=true before the refresh that uses the loaded state succeeds. The first open after a restart runs refresh in the RPC fiber (line 638), so an interruption (WS drop) or failure discards the valid persisted partials, and the next open in this process does a full rebuild. persistState also deletes the on-disk header first (line 534), so an interrupted persist drops the disk cache too. 3) StatisticsQuery.ts:640-643: a background refresh that fails within maxWaitMs surfaces as an RPC defect (orDie) instead of returning the available stale snapshot. 4) Manual Refresh goes through the same 250 ms stale-while-revalidate path (the client's fresh:true only bypasses the client handoff), so the button can return the same stale snapshot. There is no push or poll for the finished background refresh (auditor's point 3). 5) Residuals the auditor noted, which I agree with: rebuilds after any migration, an external commit, or more than max(256, n/4) dirty threads still structured-clone and Schema-decode every row in one main-thread step (StatisticsQuery.ts:409-415), which is likely hundreds of ms rather than seconds. Nothing ties STATISTICS_PARTIAL_FORMAT_VERSION to edits of processedTokenUsage.ts, statisticsAggregation.ts or forkInheritanceSql.ts, so a semantic change shipped without a migration would leave stale partials for idle threads.
implementationSketch: A) Client (main defect): turn useStatistics.ts into a per-environment cache. Better still, move it into packages/client-runtime/src/usage next to summaryCache.ts as a statisticsSnapshotCache keyed by EnvironmentId, so mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:41) can share it. In useStatistics, read usePrimaryEnvironmentId() and seed useState from cache.get(environmentId), not a global. Include environmentId in the SharedRequests key (`statistics:${environmentId}`) and in the useEffect deps. Export clearStatisticsSnapshots() and call it from clearWebHostedAccountScopedState (apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:58), next to defaultQueryClient.clear(). Optionally delete the environment's entry in clearWebHostedNodeScopedState. In ActivityView.tsx and StatisticsPanel.tsx, when error && snapshot, render a small inline notice ('Showing data from <generatedAt>; refresh failed') instead of hiding the error. Tests in useStatistics.browser.tsx: env A's snapshot is never painted for env B, and the snapshot is gone after the account teardown helper runs. B) Server: in StatisticsQuery.ts replace the `restored` boolean with a `restoredState` variable that is cleared only once a refresh has stored `cached`. Route every non-transaction call through sharedRefresh (forked into the layer scope) and Fiber.join it, with the timeout only when a stale snapshot exists. That way a caller interruption never cancels a rebuild. When stale !== undefined, map a failed join to stale (log a warning). Tests: interrupt the first getStatistics after a restart and assert that the next call re-reads only dirty threads (check the json_each scope size or worker statement count); a failing refresh with a stale snapshot returns the stale one. C) Optional: add an optional `fresh` flag to WsServerGetStatisticsRpc (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:1044) so a manual Refresh waits without maxWaitMs. Or have the client re-request once after ~1 s when generatedAt did not advance. D) Optional: decode token rows in slices with Effect.yieldNow, or compute partials in a statistics-specific worker so only partials cross the thread boundary. Fold a hash of the statistics SQL text and the aggregation source into the persisted header in place of the manual format version.
decisionReason: Keying the client cache by environment and adding one cache clear to the existing hosted teardown catalog are additive bug fixes. They do not change hosted lifecycle ownership, auth or relay semantics. The optional RPC `fresh` flag is a backward-compatible optional field, but it is not needed for the main fix.
correction: The auditor's DONE stands, but 'No blocking defect' missed a real correctness/privacy defect in the proposal-4 implementation. The module-level lastSnapshot is not keyed by environment and is not cleared on hosted node or account teardown. After a hosted node switch, or an in-page account switch, the Activity page paints the previous node's or account's statistics under the current node's label, and keeps showing them silently if the new fetch fails. Also missed: the `restored` flag discards valid persisted partials if the first refresh is interrupted, and a fast failure of the shared refresh surfaces as an RPC defect even when a stale snapshot exists.
